result:
Fixed. The test fails before the change and passes after.

## The bug

`UnixListener::bind` and `UnixStream::connect` detect an abstract socket path by checking for a leading NUL byte, then pass the **entire** byte string — NUL included — to `std::os::unix::net::SocketAddr::from_abstract_name`:

```rust
if os_str_bytes.starts_with(b"\0") {
    StdSocketAddr::from_abstract_name(os_str_bytes)?
```

But `from_abstract_name` takes the name *itself*, not the wire encoding — it prepends the NUL separator on its own. So passing `"\0aaa"` registered the abstract name `"\0aaa"`, which goes on the wire as `\0\0aaa`. The socket bound and connected fine (both sides made the same mistake consistently), which is why it stayed silent, but the registered name was wrong: `local_addr().as_abstract_name()` came back as `b"\0aaa"` instead of `b"aaa"`, and anything outside tokio addressing the socket by its documented name `\0aaa` would miss it.

## The fix

Strip the leading NUL before handing off the name, in both call sites — `tokio/src/net/unix/listener.rs:84` and `tokio/src/net/unix/stream.rs:80`:

```rust
StdSocketAddr::from_abstract_name(&os_str_bytes[1..])?
```

The index is safe: it's guarded by the `starts_with(b"\0")` check, so there is always at least one byte to drop.

## Verification

- `abstract_socket_name` in `tokio/tests/uds_stream.rs` — FAILED before, `ok` after. It now asserts `local_addr().as_abstract_name() == b"aaa"`.
- Full Unix-socket suites pass: `uds_stream`, `uds_datagram`, `uds_socket`, `uds_split`, `uds_cred` — 25 tests, 0 failures.

Two notes on scope. `UnixDatagram` has no abstract-name special-casing at all — it passes paths straight through to mio/std — so it never had this bug and needed no change. `UnixSocket::bind`/`connect` (`tokio/src/net/unix/socket.rs`) route through `socket2::SockAddr::unix`, a separate path that also doesn't call `from_abstract_name`; I left it alone as it's outside this defect, though it's worth knowing it handles abstract names by its own rules if that ever comes up.
